title.narrative: InforMEA IV – Collective Intelligence for Environmental Governance

description.narrative:
For institutions and practitioners in the environment such as MEAs and policy makers to be able to make informed decisions about their actions and perform their duties effectively, they need to have a clear understanding of the goals they are expected to achieve. This understanding needs to be provided to them in a format functional to their needs and within a reasonable timeframe. Doing justice to the complexity and broad range of information available, the Collective Intelligence for Environmental Governance Project enhances the knowledge of key stakeholders of International Environmental Law and environmental treaties. It is fully In line with the UN Secretary General’s Data Strategy of “Building a whole-of-UN ecosystem that unlocks our full data potential: For better decisions and stronger support to people and planet – in the moments that matter most”. By building a sustained and reliable shared knowledge base for better analysis and policy information this project further contributes to greater coherence in the implementation and enforcement of international environmental law.
The vision and approach of the project are entirely committed to horizontal interoperability” of information and knowledge systems among MEAs and organizations, which is also a key principle in the SG’s Data Policy towards overcoming misaligned standards, and mixed-quality data. A core component/tool of this project is the InforMEA Portal - which is the online home of Multilateral Environmental Agreements (MEAs). This website reduces the time and effort of stakeholders to obtain relevant knowledge and process available information. The Portal and the InforMEA Initiative behind it have been financially supported by the European Union since 2014. Its two result streams focus on 1) synergetic collaboration across all global MEAs and their Partners around sharing knowledge through interconnected information systems and associated best practices, and 2) curating and presenting knowledge and information from MEAs and their partners in a user-friendly way for stakeholders of international and national environmental law and governance. For this upcoming phase, the re-focus of this component will be on services to the MEA stakeholders in the narrower sense, as guided by the recommendations of the latest project evaluation of this component (attached).
Secondly, a component of the project is dedicated to the related, partly more recent knowledge tools of the Environmental Governance Sub-programme supported by this project including the Law and Environment Assistance Platform and the Judicial Portal on the Environment, the emerging Air pollution policy tracker on air quality and many related legislation toolkits and topical sections including on plastics and marine litter.
Lastly, the Collective Intelligence (CI) project is also committed, in component 3 to enhancing the interface between normative knowledge and legislative content and scientific and statistical stakeholders catered for by the World Environment Situation Room and other key tools. In this regard, enhancing the flow of content from Collective Intelligence tools and its contributing data sources to WESR and other divisions’ flagship tools within UNEP will be a third component of this project, which will be co-steered by the Digital Transformation Sub-programme.
